seg-004.note: lint run: a linter's own aggregate summary line ('Found 3 errors (3 fixed, 0 remaining)') with no exception traceback — the canonical skip. The discriminator from seg-006 (also an in-segment resolved error, but 'keep') is traceback-vs-summary-line, not resolved-vs-unresolved: a 'the error count came back to 0' rule alone would wrongly skip seg-006 too, since it also resolves within the segment.

seg-006.note: ACCEPTED FALSE POSITIVE: a typo-error segment trips the error rule — its tool_result contains an actual exception traceback (NameError), not just a linter's summary line like seg-004's — so a traceback-vs-summary-line rule keeps it distinct from seg-004's skip; recall-tuning means we pay NPU time here rather than risk skipping real errors. Its golden is non-empty (f-006-01): under adr/0003 the distiller compresses whatever a 'keep' triage sends it and does not re-judge durability, so an ACCEPTED FALSE POSITIVE here costs NPU time and produces a faithful finding, not an empty array — see the Post-review amendment on Task 4 in docs/plans/exec/2026-08-04-e1-corpus-and-privacy-metric.md.

seg-007.note: ACCEPTED FALSE POSITIVE: grep output containing the word 'error'; a keyword triage cannot tell mentions from failures, and skipping on this rule would also skip real failures. Its golden is non-empty (f-007-01) for the same adr/0003 reason as seg-006.
